initial_simplification: Scientists who study the brain, called neuroscientists, use special machines to take pictures of the brain. One of these machines is called functional magnetic resonance imaging, or fMRI for short. They use these pictures to learn how the brain works when we do things like remember new information, make choices, or understand language.

source_text: Neuroscientists have long utilized sophisticated imaging techniques, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), to investigate the intricate neural mechanisms underlying cognitive processes like memory formation, decision-making, and language comprehension.
target_text: Scientists who study the brain use advanced techniques to see how our brain works. One of these techniques is called functional magnetic resonance imaging, or fMRI. They use fMRI to learn about important tasks our brain does, like how we remember things, make choices, and understand language.
